questionsToConsider: Which kinds of work does your team take on, and where should other requests go?
What counts as urgent for you, and who is on hand to respond to it?
Do requests need a manager's approval before work starts?
Would a location or asset question help your team find the problem faster?
guide.howToUseResponses: Check the urgent requests first and reply the same day, even if only to say who has it. Triage the rest weekly using the impact and deadline answers: a fault affecting customers outranks a new idea for one person. Export the responses to CSV each month and count requests by kind, since a steady stream of the same fault is a sign to fix the cause rather than the symptom.
customizeSteps: Change the team question to a dropdown of your departments or sites if you want cleaner reporting.
Put how to reach the team directly in the urgent ending, so people know what to do if things get worse.
Share the link wherever requests used to arrive, such as your intranet or team chat, and reply to ad hoc asks with it.

faqs.q: What should a work request form include?
faqs.a: Who is asking, what needs doing, why it matters, who it affects and when it is needed. A photo or screenshot often saves a follow-up question.

faqs.q: Is a work request the same as a work order?
faqs.a: Not quite. A work request is someone asking for a job; a work order is the job once it has been approved and assigned. Many teams turn requests into work orders after triage.

faqs.q: How do I handle urgent work requests?
faqs.a: This form asks whether anyone is unable to work, and sends those requests to a separate ending that says they will be handled first. Make sure someone checks for them daily.

faqs.q: Can I add different questions for maintenance or IT work?
faqs.a: Yes. Copy it with Use this template and add request types, each with its own follow-up questions through branching.
